Filtrations allow us to establish the decidability of our systems of modal logic by showing that they have the finite model property, that is, that any formula that is true (false) in a model is also true (false) in a finite model. Filtrations are defined relative to sets of formulas which are closed under subformulas. Definition. A set Gamma of formulas is closed under subformulas if it contains every subformula of a formula in Gamma . Further, Gamma is modally closed if it is closed under subformulas and moreover formula A belongs to Gamma implies necessarily A and possibly A both belong to Gamma . End definition. For instance, given a formula A , the set of all its sub-formulas is closed under sub-formulas. When we're defining a filtration of a model through the set of sub-formulas of formula A , it will have the property we're after: it makes formula A true (false) if and only if the original model does. The set of worlds of a filtration of model M through Gamma is defined as the set of all equivalence classes of the following equivalence relation. Definition. Let model M is the ordered triple of world set W, accessibility relation R, and valuation V and suppose Gamma is closed under sub-formulas. Define a relation the filtration equivalence relation on world set W to hold of any two worlds that make the same formulas from Gamma true, that is: Displayed expression. World u is equivalent to world v if and only if, for every formula A in Gamma, A is true at u in model M exactly when A is true at v in model M. End displayed expression. The equivalence class the equivalence class of world w under the filtration equivalence relation of a world world w , or the equivalence class of world w for short, is the set of all worlds the filtration equivalence relation -equivalent to world w : Displayed expression. the equivalence class of w is the set of all v equivalent to w. End displayed expression. End definition. Proposition. Given model M and Gamma , the filtration equivalence relation as defined above is an equivalence relation, that is, it is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. End proposition. Proof. The relation the filtration equivalence relation is reflexive, since world w makes exactly the same formulas from Gamma true as itself. It is symmetric since if world u makes the same formulas from Gamma true as world v , the same holds for world v and world u . It is also transitive, since if world u makes the same formulas from Gamma true as world v , and world v as world w , then world u makes the same formulas from Gamma true as world w . End proof. The relation the filtration equivalence relation , like any equivalence relation, divides world set W into partitions, that is, subsets of world set W which are pairwise disjoint, and together cover all of world set W . Every world w belongs to world set W is an element of one of the partitions, namely of the equivalence class of world w , since world w is equivalent to world w . A system Sigma of modal logic is said to have the finite model property if whenever a formula A is true at a world in a model of Sigma then formula A is true at a world in a finite model of Sigma . End definition. Proposition. K has the finite model property. End proposition. Proof. K is the set of valid formulas, that is, any model is a model of K. By the Filtration Theorem preserving truth of formulas in Gamma , if formula A is true at world w in model M , then formula A is true at world w in model M star for any filtration of model M through the set Gamma of sub-formulas of formula A . Any formula only has finitely many sub-formulas, so Gamma is finite. By the proposition bounding the size of a filtration , the cardinality of world set W star is at most two to the power n , where n is the number of formulas in Gamma . And since K imposes no restriction on models, model M star is a K-model. End proof. Source anomaly note. Source world-label caveat. This filtration proof writes world w rather than equivalence class w on the filtered-model side. The formula is retained and no bracketed class is silently inserted. Original source remains available in Source view. End note. To show that a logic L has the finite model property via filtrations it is essential that the filtration of an L-model is itself a L-model. Often this requires a fair bit of work, and not any filtration yields a L-model. However, for universal models, this still holds. Proposition. Let class U of universal models be the class of universal models (see the equivalence between S five models and universal models used here ) and the class of finite universal models the class of all finite universal models. Then any formula A is valid in class U of universal models if and only if it is valid in the class of finite universal models . End proposition. Proof. Finite universal models are universal models, so the left-to-right direction is trivial. For the right-to left direction, suppose that formula A is false at some world world w in a universal model model M . Let Gamma contain formula A as well as all of its subformulas; clearly Gamma is finite. Take a filtration model M star of model M ; then model M star is finite by the proposition bounding the size of a filtration , and by the Filtration Theorem preserving truth of formulas in Gamma , formula A is false at the equivalence class of world w in model M star . By the proposition reducing universal-model validity to finite universal models , it is true at a world in a finite universal model (namely the filtration of the model through the set of sub-formulas of formula A ). End definition. Proposition. K has the finite model property. End proposition. Proof. K is the set of valid formulas, that is, any model is a model of K. By the Filtration Theorem preserving truth of formulas in Gamma , if formula A is true at world w in model M , then formula A is true at world w in model M star for any filtration of model M through the set Gamma of sub-formulas of formula A . Any formula only has finitely many sub-formulas, so Gamma is finite. By the proposition bounding the size of a filtration , the cardinality of world set W star is at most two to the power n , where n is the number of formulas in Gamma . And since K imposes no restriction on models, model M star is a K-model. End proof. Source anomaly note. Source world-label caveat. This filtration proof writes world w rather than equivalence class w on the filtered-model side. The formula is retained and no bracketed class is silently inserted. Original source remains available in Source view. End note. To show that a logic L has the finite model property via filtrations it is essential that the filtration of an L-model is itself a L-model. Often this requires a fair bit of work, and not any filtration yields a L-model. However, for universal models, this still holds. Proposition. Let class U of universal models be the class of universal models (see the equivalence between S five models and universal models used here ) and the class of finite universal models the class of all finite universal models. Then any formula A is valid in class U of universal models if and only if it is valid in the class of finite universal models . End proposition. Proof. Finite universal models are universal models, so the left-to-right direction is trivial. For the right-to left direction, suppose that formula A is false at some world world w in a universal model model M . Let Gamma contain formula A as well as all of its subformulas; clearly Gamma is finite. Take a filtration model M star of model M ; then model M star is finite by the proposition bounding the size of a filtration , and by the Filtration Theorem preserving truth of formulas in Gamma , formula A is false at the equivalence class of world w in model M star . It remains to observe that model M star is also universal: given world u and world v , by hypothesis world v is accessible from world u under accessibility relation R and by the definition of a filtration the accessibility conditions in the definition of a filtration , also the equivalence class of world v is accessible from the equivalence class of world u under accessibility relation R star . End proof. Corollary. Sfive has the finite model property. End corollary. Proof. By the equivalence between S five models and universal models used here , if formula A is true at a world in some reflexive and euclidean model then it is true at a world in a universal model. By the proposition reducing universal-model validity to finite universal models , it is true at a world in a finite universal model (namely the filtration of the model through the set of sub-formulas of formula A ). Every universal model is also reflexive and euclidean; so formula A is true at a world in a finite reflexive euclidean model. End proof. Exercise. Show that any filtration of a serial or reflexive model is also serial or reflexive (respectively). End exercise. This exercise remains unsolved. Exercise. Find a non-symmetric (non-transitive, non-euclidean) filtration of a symmetric (transitive, euclidean) model. End exercise. This exercise remains unsolved. End section.

listen_text: Section. Sfive is Decidable. The finite model property gives us an easy way to show that systems of modal logic given by schemas are decidable (that is, that there is a computable procedure to determine whether a formula is derivable in the system or not). Theorem. Sfive is decidable. End theorem. Proof. Let formula A be given, and suppose the propositional variables occurring in formula A are among p sub one , and so on, p sub k . Since for each n there are only finitely many models with n worlds assigning a value to p sub one , and so on, p sub k , we can enumerate, in parallel, all the theorems of Sfive by generating proofs in some systematic way; and all the models containing one , two , and so on worlds and checking whether formula A fails at a world in some such model. Eventually one of the two parallel processes will give an answer, as by the general canonical-model determination theorem and the finite model property corollary for S five , either formula A is derivable or it fails in a finite universal model. End proof. Source anomaly note. Source proof caveat. The proposed countermodel lane says to enumerate all finite models, although the final justification requires failure in a finite universal model. Searching unrestricted models could stop on a countermodel irrelevant to S five validity. The argument is preserved without a repaired decision procedure.
